## Find the mean
The normal curve is symmetric, so the mean is halfway between 7.2 and 8.4.
\mu &= \frac{7.2 + 8.4}{2}
&= \frac{15.6}{2}
&= 7.8
## Find the standard deviation
The empirical rule says 68% lies within one standard deviation of the mean, so 8.4 is $\mu + \sigma$.
\sigma &= 8.4 - 7.8
&= 0.6
## Find the left-hand missing value
The left box is two standard deviations below the mean.
\mu - 2\sigma &= 7.8 - 1.2
&= 6.6
## Find the right-hand missing value
The right box is two standard deviations above the mean.
\mu + 2\sigma &= 7.8 + 1.2
&= 9.0
ANSWER: 6.6,\ 7.8,\ 9.0

## Place 9 hours on the curve
From part (i), 9.0 is $\mu + 2\sigma$.
## Use the 95% rule
The empirical rule says 95% lies between $\mu - 2\sigma$ and $\mu + 2\sigma$.
100 - 95 &= 5
5% lies outside, split equally between the two tails.
\frac{5}{2} &= 2.5
## Find the percentage below 9.0
Below 9.0 is the left tail (2.5%) plus the middle 95%.
2.5 + 95 &= 97.5
## Find the percentage of at least 9 hours
100 - 97.5 &= 2.5
ANSWER: 2.5\%

## (i) Use the complement
Not getting enough sleep is the opposite of getting enough, so the probabilities add to 1.
P(\text{not enough}) &= 1 - 0.1
&= 0.9
## (ii) List what must happen
Not enough on night 1, not enough on night 2, then enough on night 3 (Tuesday).
## (ii) Multiply the probabilities
The nights are independent, so multiply.
P &= 0.9 \times 0.9 \times 0.1
&= 0.81 \times 0.1
&= 0.081
ANSWER: \text{(i) } 0.9, \quad \text{(ii) } 0.081

## Set up the bisector of angle Y
Place the compass point on $Y$ and draw one arc that crosses both sides $YX$ and $YZ$.
## Find a second point on the bisector from Y
Keep the same compass width. Put the point on each place where the arc crossed a side, and draw two small arcs that cross each other inside the triangle.
Draw a straight line from $Y$ through the crossing point. This is the bisector of $\angle XYZ$.
## Bisect a second angle in the same way
Repeat at $Z$: one arc across $ZY$ and $ZX$, then two crossing arcs, then a line from $Z$ through the crossing point.
Two bisectors are enough, because all three meet at the same point.
## Mark the incentre
The incentre $I$ is where the bisectors cross. It is the centre of the circle that touches all three sides.
ANSWER: \text{Incentre } I = \text{ meeting point of the angle bisectors}

## Find the scale factor
$[BC]$ maps to $[DE]$, so the scale factor is image length divided by object length.
k &= \frac{|DE|}{|BC|}
&= \frac{14}{4}
&= 3.5
## Find |AE|
$[AE]$ is the image of $[AC]$, so multiply $|AC|$ by $k$.
|AE| &= k \times |AC|
&= 3.5 \times 6
&= 21
## Subtract |AC| to get |CE|
$C$ lies on $[AE]$, so $|CE| = |AE| - |AC|$.
|CE| &= |AE| - |AC|
&= 21 - 6
&= 15
ANSWER: |CE| = 15

## Square the scale factor for areas
Areas change by $k^2$, where $k = 3.5$.
k^2 &= 3.5^2
&= 12.25
## Multiply the area of ABC
\text{Area } ADE &= 11 \times k^2
&= 11 \times 12.25
&= 134.75
ANSWER: 134.75 \text{ units}^2

## Put the stem for each value in its row
The stem is the tens (and hundreds) part. The leaf is the units digit.
Sort the leaves in each row so they increase moving away from the stem.
## Fill in the before-exercise leaves (left side)
$60, 65, 67, 68$ go in row 6 as leaves $0, 5, 7, 8$.
$70, 76, 77$ go in row 7 as leaves $0, 6, 7$.
$83, 88, 89$ go in row 8 as leaves $3, 8, 9$.
## Fill in the after-exercise leaves (right side)
$71, 79$ in row 7. $81, 83, 87$ in row 8. $91$ in row 9.
$102, 108$ in row 10 as leaves $2, 8$. $113, 118$ in row 11 as leaves $3, 8$.
ANSWER: \text{Completed back-to-back plot (see diagram)}

## Add the heart rates after exercise
\sum x &= 71+81+79+108+91+83+102+113+118+87
&= 933
## Divide by the number of values to find the mean
There are $n = 10$ values.
\mu &= \frac{\sum x}{n}
&= \frac{933}{10}
&= 93.3
## Square each value and add
\sum x^2 &= 71^2+81^2+79^2+108^2+91^2+83^2+102^2+113^2+118^2+87^2
&= 5041+6561+6241+11664+8281+6889+10404+12769+13924+7569
&= 89343
## Find the variance
Use $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \mu^2$.
\sigma^2 &= \frac{89343}{10} - 93.3^2
&= 8934.3 - 8704.89
&= 229.41
## Take the square root
\sigma &= \sqrt{229.41}
&= 15.146
&= 15.1
ANSWER: \text{Mean} = 93.3, \quad \sigma = 15.1

## Compare the spread on each side of the plot
Before exercise the rates run from $60$ to $89$, a range of $29$.
After exercise they run from $71$ to $118$, a range of $47$.
The after-exercise values are more spread out, so the standard deviation increased.
ANSWER: \text{Increased: there is a greater spread in the data}

## Read the scatter plot
As the heart rate before exercise goes up, the heart rate after exercise goes up.
The points lie close to a rising straight line, so there is strong positive correlation.
A strong positive value is $0.9$. ($0.3$ would be a weak scatter, and the negatives would slope downwards).
ANSWER: r = 0.9 \text{ (strong positive correlation)}

## Use the margin of error formula
Margin of error for a proportion is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, with $n = 355$.
\text{Margin} &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{355}}
&= 0.05307
&= 5.307\%
To 1 decimal place this is $5.3\%$.
ANSWER: \text{Margin of error} = 5.3\%

## Divide the number who finished under 25 minutes by the sample size
\hat p &= \frac{96}{355}
&= 0.27042
## Convert to a percentage
\text{Percentage} &= 0.27042 \times 100
&= 27.042\%
&= 27\%
ANSWER: 27\%

## Form the interval around the sample percentage
The claim is tested using $\hat p \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, with $\hat p = 27\%$ and margin $5.3\%$.
## Find the lower limit
27 - 5.3 &= 21.7
## Find the upper limit
27 + 5.3 &= 32.3
## Compare 24% with the interval
21.7 &\le p \le 32.3
$24\%$ lies between $21.7\%$ and $32.3\%$.
## State the conclusion and reason
Conclusion: there is no evidence of a change. The percentage of runners finishing under 25 minutes is not shown to have changed since 2019.
Reason: $24\%$ is inside the interval, so it is within the confidence interval.
ANSWER: \text{No change: } 24\% \text{ lies within } 21.7\% \le p \le 32.3\%

## Use the Theorem of Pythagoras
$[GF]$ is the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle $FHG$.
|GF|^2 &= |GH|^2 + |FH|^2
&= 1.4^2 + 3^2
&= 1.96 + 9
&= 10.96
## Take the square root
|GF| &= \sqrt{10.96}
&= 3.3106
&= 3.3
ANSWER: |GF| = 3.3 \text{ m}

## Use tangent in triangle FHG
Opposite side to the angle is $|FH| = 3$ and the adjacent side is $|GH| = 1.4$.
\tan(\angle FGH) &= \frac{3}{1.4}
## Find the angle
\angle FGH &= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{1.4}\right)
&= 64.98^\circ
&= 65^\circ
ANSWER: \angle FGH = 65^\circ

## Find the height of K
$K$ is halfway up the sign, so $|KH| = 3 \div 2 = 1.5$.
## Find the angle KGH
\tan(\angle KGH) &= \frac{1.5}{1.4}
\angle KGH &= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1.5}{1.4}\right)
&= 46.97^\circ
&= 47^\circ
## Compare with half of angle FGH
\tfrac{1}{2}(65^\circ) &= 32.5^\circ
$47^\circ \ne 32.5^\circ$, so Mairead is not correct.
ANSWER: \text{No: } \angle KGH = 47^\circ \ne 32.5^\circ

## Write down the sine rule
$\theta$ is opposite $|AB| = 12$, and the angle $37^\circ$ is opposite $|AC| = 10$.
\frac{12}{\sin\theta} &= \frac{10}{\sin 37^\circ}
## Rearrange for sin θ
\sin\theta &= \frac{12\sin 37^\circ}{10}
&= 0.72218
## Find the angle
In the diagram $\theta$ is acute, so take the calculator value.
\theta &= \sin^{-1}(0.72218)
&= 46.23^\circ
&= 46^\circ
ANSWER: \theta = 46^\circ

## Write down the cosine rule
Angle $110^\circ$ is between $|CF|$ and $|EF|$, opposite $|CE|$.
|CE|^2 &= 22^2 + 11.8^2 - 2(22)(11.8)\cos 110^\circ
## Work out each part
|CE|^2 &= 484 + 139.24 - 519.2\cos 110^\circ
&= 623.24 - 519.2(-0.34202)
&= 623.24 + 177.58
&= 800.82
## Take the square root
|CE| &= \sqrt{800.82}
&= 28.30
&= 28.3
ANSWER: |CE| = 28.3 \text{ cm}

## Find the area of triangle CEF
Use $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ with the sides $22$ and $11.8$ and the angle $110^\circ$ between them.
\text{Area } CEF &= \tfrac{1}{2}(22)(11.8)\sin 110^\circ
&= 129.8 \sin 110^\circ
&= 121.97
## Double it, since CDEF is symmetrical about CE
\text{Total area} &= 2 \times 121.97
&= 243.94
&= 244
ANSWER: 244 \text{ cm}^2

## Count the choices for part (i)
Multiply the number of options for each choice.
7 \times 4 \times 2 &= 56
## Add an extra flavour
8 \times 4 \times 2 &= 64
## Add an extra topping
7 \times 5 \times 2 &= 70
## Compare
$70 > 64$, so an extra topping gives more choices.
ANSWER: \text{(i) } 56 \text{ choices; (ii) extra topping}

## Find how many bought vanilla or a cone
$45$ bought neither, so the rest bought at least one.
100 - 45 &= 55
## Find the overlap
Adding $V$ and $C$ counts the overlap twice, so subtract the total.
42 + 37 - 55 &= 24
## Find the parts of each circle outside the overlap
42 - 24 &= 18
37 - 24 &= 13
ANSWER: V \text{ only } 18, \; V \cap C = 24, \; C \text{ only } 13

## Write down the expected value formula
Multiply each sales figure by its probability and add.
## Substitute
E &= 150(0.3) + 200(0.45) + 450(0.25)
&= 45 + 90 + 112.5
&= 247.5
ANSWER: \text{€}247.50

## Find the angle theta
The angles around the centre add to $360^\circ$.
\theta &= 360 - 2(70)
&= 360 - 140
&= 220
## Find the arc length
The arc is $\frac{\theta}{360}$ of the circumference $2\pi r$.
s &= \frac{220}{360} \times 2\pi(20)
&= 76.79
&= 76.8
ANSWER: \theta = 220^\circ, \quad s = 76.8 \text{ cm}

## Use tangent in the right-angled triangle
The side $l$ is opposite the $70^\circ$ angle and the radius $20$ is adjacent.
\tan 70^\circ &= \frac{l}{20}
## Make l the subject
l &= 20\tan 70^\circ
&= 54.95
&= 55
ANSWER: l = 55 \text{ cm}

## Use the surface area of a sphere
\text{SA} &= 4\pi r^2
&= 4\pi(3.27)^2
&= 4\pi(10.6929)
&= 134.3709
&= 134.37
ANSWER: 134.37 \text{ cm}^2

## Find the volume of the whole ball
Volume of a sphere is $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, with $r_1 = 3.4$.
V_1 &= \tfrac{4}{3}\pi(3.4)^3
&= 164.636
## Find the volume of the air-filled centre
V_2 &= \tfrac{4}{3}\pi(3.1)^3
&= 124.788
## Subtract to get the rubber layer
\text{Rubber} &= V_1 - V_2
&= 164.636 - 124.788
&= 39.848
&= 39.85
ANSWER: 39.85 \text{ cm}^3

## Show the height
Each ball has diameter $2 \times 3.4 = 6.8$ cm, and three balls sit one on top of the other.
h &= 3 \times 6.8
&= 20.4
So $h = 20.4$ cm.
## Find the volume of the cylinder
The cylinder radius equals the ball radius $3.4$.
V &= \pi r^2 h
&= \pi(3.4)^2(20.4)
&= 740.86
&= 741
ANSWER: V = 741 \text{ cm}^3

## Find the dimensions of the box
The box is as wide as one ball, $6.8$ cm, in both directions. Its height is $20.4$ cm.
## Find the area of each type of face
The top and bottom faces are $6.8 \times 6.8$.
6.8 \times 6.8 &= 46.24
The four side faces are $6.8 \times 20.4$.
6.8 \times 20.4 &= 138.72
## Add up all six faces
\text{SA} &= 2(46.24) + 4(138.72)
&= 92.48 + 554.88
&= 647.36
ANSWER: 647.36 \text{ cm}^2

## Rewrite the modulus as a double inequality
$|A| \le k$ means $A$ is between $-k$ and $k$.
|x-3| &\le 12
-12 \le x - 3 &\le 12
## Add 3 to every part
-12 + 3 \le x - 3 + 3 &\le 12 + 3
-9 \le x &\le 15
ANSWER: -9 \le x \le 15

## Divide the cubic by the factor $(2x+3)$
Since $(2x+3)$ is a factor, $4x^3 - 12x^2 - 7x + 30 = (2x+3)(ax^2 + bx + c)$.
The $x^3$ term: $2x \times ax^2 = 4x^3$, so $a = 2$.
The constant term: $3 \times c = 30$, so $c = 10$.
4x^3 - 12x^2 - 7x + 30 &= (2x+3)(2x^2 + bx + 10)
## Expand the right-hand side
(2x+3)(2x^2 + bx + 10) &= 4x^3 + 2bx^2 + 20x + 6x^2 + 3bx + 30
&= 4x^3 + (2b + 6)x^2 + (20 + 3b)x + 30
## Compare the $x$ terms to find $b$
The $x$ term on the left of the cubic is $-7x$.
20 + 3b &= -7
3b &= -27
b &= -9
## Write the quadratic factor and set it to zero
2x^2 - 9x + 10 &= 0
## Factorise the quadratic
Find two numbers with product $2 \times 10 = 20$ and sum $-9$: they are $-4$ and $-5$.
2x^2 - 9x + 10 &= 2x^2 - 4x - 5x + 10
&= 2x(x - 2) - 5(x - 2)
&= (2x - 5)(x - 2)
## Solve the given factor $2x + 3 = 0$
2x + 3 &= 0
x &= -\frac{3}{2}
## Solve $2x - 5 = 0$
2x - 5 &= 0
x &= \frac{5}{2}
## Solve $x - 2 = 0$
x - 2 &= 0
x &= 2
ANSWER: x = -\frac{3}{2}, \quad x = \frac{5}{2}, \quad x = 2

## Differentiate each term separately
The derivative of the constant $6$ is $0$, and the derivative of $x^2$ is $2x$.
For $\sin 4x$ use the chain rule: the derivative of $\sin u$ is $\cos u$, times the derivative of $u = 4x$, which is $4$.
f'(x) &= 0 + 2x + 4\cos 4x
&= 2x + 4\cos 4x
ANSWER: f'(x) = 2x + 4\cos 4x

## Find the slope of the tangent at $x = 0$
The slope of the tangent is $f'(0)$.
f'(0) &= 2(0) + 4\cos(4(0))
&= 0 + 4\cos 0
$\cos 0 = 1$.
&= 4
## Find the $y$-value at $x = 0$
f(0) &= 6 + (0)^2 + \sin(4(0))
&= 6 + 0 + 0
&= 6
So the point of contact is $(0, 6)$.
## Substitute into $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$
y - 6 &= 4(x - 0)
y - 6 &= 4x
## Rearrange into the form $ax + by + c = 0$
Move $y$ and $-6$ to the other side so the right-hand side is $0$.
0 &= 4x - y + 6
4x - y + 6 &= 0
ANSWER: 4x - y + 6 = 0

## (i) Find the slope of each segment
$g'(x)$ is the slope of the graph. Find the slope of each line segment.
\text{First segment, } (0,0) \text{ to } (3,1): \quad m &= \frac{1 - 0}{3 - 0}
&= \frac{1}{3}
\text{Second segment, } (3,1) \text{ to } (4,4): \quad m &= \frac{4 - 1}{4 - 3}
&= 3
Only the second segment has slope greater than $2$, so $g'(x) > 2$ for $3 < x \le 4$.
## (ii) Find $g(3)$ from the graph
Go up from $x = 3$ to the graph at $(3, 1)$ (blue dashed line on the diagram). So $g(3) = 1$.
g(3) &= 1
## (ii) Find $g(1)$, the value of $g(g(3))$
Now find $g(1)$. Go across from $(3, 1)$ to the line $y = x$ at $(1, 1)$. Go straight down to the graph at $(1, \frac{1}{3})$, then across to the $y$-axis.
The first segment passes through $(0,0)$ with slope $\frac{1}{3}$, so it has equation $y = \frac{1}{3}x$.
g(g(3)) &= g(1)
&= \frac{1}{3}(1)
&= \frac{1}{3}
## (iii) Swap the $x$ and $y$ coordinates of key points
Reflecting in $y = x$ swaps each point $(x, y)$ to $(y, x)$.
(0, 0) &\to (0, 0)
(3, 1) &\to (1, 3)
(4, 4) &\to (4, 4)
## (iii) Draw and label $g^{-1}$
Join $(0,0)$ to $(1,3)$, then $(1,3)$ to $(4,4)$, with straight lines.
Label the new graph $y = g^{-1}(x)$ (blue in the diagram).
ANSWER: 3 < x \le 4, \quad g(g(3)) = \frac{1}{3}, \quad g^{-1} \text{ joins } (0,0),\ (1,3),\ (4,4)

## Identify the outer and inner functions
$f(x) = u^{28}$ where $u = 3x^5 - 4$. Use the chain rule: $f'(x) = 28u^{27} \times \frac{du}{dx}$.
## Differentiate the inner function
\frac{du}{dx} &= 15x^4
## Multiply the two results together
f'(x) &= 28(3x^5 - 4)^{27} \times 15x^4
ANSWER: f'(x) = 28(3x^5 - 4)^{27}(15x^4)

## Integrate $e^{5x}$
$\int e^{ax}\,dx = \frac{1}{a}e^{ax}$, so with $a = 5$:
\int_0^k e^{5x}\,dx &= \left[\frac{1}{5}e^{5x}\right]_0^k
## Substitute the limits and set equal to 9
\frac{1}{5}e^{5k} - \frac{1}{5}e^{5(0)} &= 9
$e^0 = 1$.
\frac{1}{5}e^{5k} - \frac{1}{5} &= 9
## Isolate $e^{5k}$
Multiply both sides by 5.
e^{5k} - 1 &= 45
Add 1 to both sides.
e^{5k} &= 46
## Take natural logs and solve for $k$
5k &= \ln 46
k &= \frac{\ln 46}{5}
This is in the form $\frac{\ln a}{b}$ with $a = 46$, $b = 5$.
ANSWER: k = \frac{\ln 46}{5}

## Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator
The conjugate of $4-5i$ is $4+5i$. Multiplying top and bottom by it does not change the value.
\frac{2+3i}{4-5i} &= \frac{2+3i}{4-5i}\times\frac{4+5i}{4+5i}
&= \frac{(2+3i)(4+5i)}{(4-5i)(4+5i)}
## Expand the top line
(2+3i)(4+5i) &= 8 + 10i + 12i + 15i^2
&= 8 + 22i + 15i^2
Use $i^2=-1$.
&= 8 + 22i - 15
&= -7 + 22i
## Expand the bottom line
(4-5i)(4+5i) &= 16 + 20i - 20i - 25i^2
&= 16 - 25i^2
&= 16 + 25
&= 41
## Write in the form a + bi
\frac{2+3i}{4-5i} &= \frac{-7+22i}{41}
&= -\frac{7}{41} + \frac{22}{41}i
ANSWER: -\frac{7}{41} + \frac{22}{41}i

## Apply de Moivre's theorem to the left side
De Moivre's theorem: $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^n = \cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta$.
(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2 &= \cos 2\theta + i\sin 2\theta
## Expand the square directly
(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2 &= (\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)
&= \cos^2\theta + 2i\cos\theta\sin\theta + i^2\sin^2\theta
## Replace i squared with minus 1
(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2 &= \cos^2\theta + 2i\cos\theta\sin\theta - \sin^2\theta
&= (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta) + i(2\cos\theta\sin\theta)
## Equate the real parts
Both expressions equal $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2$, so their real parts are equal.
\cos 2\theta + i\sin 2\theta &= (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta) + i(2\cos\theta\sin\theta)
\cos 2\theta &= \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta
ANSWER: \cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta

## Write -64i in polar form
$-64i$ lies on the negative imaginary axis, 64 units below the origin.
r &= 64
\theta &= \frac{3\pi}{2}
z^6 &= 64\left(\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\right)\right)
## Take the sixth root using de Moivre's theorem
Raise to the power $\tfrac16$: divide each angle by 6 and take the sixth root of the modulus.
z &= 64^{\frac{1}{6}}\left[\cos\left(\frac{3\pi/2 + 2n\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{3\pi/2 + 2n\pi}{6}\right)\right]
The sixth root of $64$ is $2$, because $2^6 = 64$.
&= 2\left[\cos\left(\frac{3\pi/2 + 2n\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{3\pi/2 + 2n\pi}{6}\right)\right]
Divide each term of the angle by $6$.
\frac{3\pi/2 + 2n\pi}{6} &= \frac{3\pi}{12} + \frac{2n\pi}{6}
&= \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{n\pi}{3}
z &= 2\left[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{n\pi}{3}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{n\pi}{3}\right)\right]
## First root: n = 0
z &= 2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
&= 2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\right)
&= \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}i
## Second root: n = 3
\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{3\pi}{3} &= \frac{\pi}{4} + \pi
&= \frac{5\pi}{4}
z &= 2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)
$\cos\frac{5\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\sin\frac{5\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
&= 2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\right)
&= -\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}i
ANSWER: z = \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}i \quad\text{and}\quad z = -\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}i
